description:
FILED s470bi (Opus, 2026-09-05) while probing #1084.  PRE-EXISTING, SILENT.

perl's `do FILE` populates %INC with the path it ran, so a LATER `require` of
the same path is a no-op.  PCL's `do FILE` does not, so the `require` runs the
file a SECOND time -- every side effect happens twice.

REPRO (scratch/s469bi/p1084/r.pl; tiny2.pl sets $main::v = 42 and
$main::len):

    do "./tiny2.pl" or die;
    print "do:      v=$main::v\n";
    $main::v = 0;
    require "./tiny2.pl";
    print "require: v=$main::v\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  do: v=42   require: v=0     (the require is a no-op)
  PCL:          do: v=42   require: v=42    (the file ran again)

Doubling a load is the classic way a module's BEGIN-time registration, an
`our @ISA` push or a counter goes wrong; nothing is printed either way.

WHAT PERL DOES, exactly (probe before fixing): `do FILE` sets
`$INC{FILE}` -- keyed by the STRING the caller wrote, not the resolved path --
and it does so whether the file compiled or not (perldoc -f do: "the file is
not added to %INC" is FALSE since 5.x for the success case; measure it).
`require` then skips it.  A failed `do` sets `$INC{FILE}` to undef in some
versions; probe 5.40.3 and match what it does.

WHERE: `p-do` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp -- the same function #1084 fixed the read
of.  The `require` side already consults %INC (`p-require`), so the fix is one
write in the `do` path plus the probe above.

=== DONE (s470br) ===
SHIPPED.  One write in `p-do`, after the READ and before the compile -- which is
where perl puts it, probed rather than guessed: a file that compiles and then
DIES still leaves the entry, so does one that returns FALSE, and one that could
not be OPENED leaves none.  The key is THE STRING THE CALLER WROTE, the value the
path opened (spelled the way p-require-file spells it -- an absolute native path,
not perl's literal string, the same divergence `require "./file.pl"` already
had).  `do` itself never CONSULTS %INC (two `do`s run a file twice, probed).

Nine of nine probe rows now match perl key for key, including the @INC-search
spelling and the compile-error case.  Guards: two rows in Pl/t/use-require-01.t
through its own `inc_agrees`, which runs the program under REAL PERL and
compares, so the expectation is perl's answer by construction; both FAIL on a
`git archive f728637` extraction of the base.  Companion op/do.t 66/7 XDIFF
unchanged, ROW DIFF 0/0/0/0.  ir-spec Â§9 gains the normative paragraph.
Runtime-only: no emission change.
subject: do FILE does not populate %INC, so a later require of the same path runs the file a SECOND time (perl: a no-op)
